prediction_ref.short_label: On-device LLM silicon ships 1-PFLOP deskside + sandbox-runtime specs by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Microsoft's Surface RTX Spark Dev Box is the most concrete deskside artifact the prediction has drawn yet. Announced at Build, it turns the RTX Spark Grace-Blackwell superchip into a developer workstation: a Blackwell RTX GPU paired with a Grace CPU and 128 GB of unified memory delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI compute, enough to run 120B-plus-parameter models at a 1-million-token context entirely locally. It ships as a Secured-core PC running Windows 11 Pro with WSL 2 pre-configured for GPU passthrough and CUDA, managed through Entra ID and Intune, and bundles Foundry Local, Microsoft's roughly 20 MB on-device runtime that reached GA in April and added live audio transcription, on-device embeddings and Qwen 3.5 Vision inference, a WebGPU execution provider, and Linux ARM64 support in its late-May 1.1 and 1.2 updates. That pairs a petaflop-class deskside part with a named on-device runtime sized to run frontier-class open models off the cloud, which is the exact silicon-plus-runtime bundle the prediction tracks. The distance to the forward state is that this is still Microsoft and Nvidia, the same pairing that anchored the June 1 trigger, rather than one of the named peer silicon stacks (Apple, Qualcomm, AMD, Intel) publishing a matching deskside spec, and there is no industry-body profile naming the petaflop-plus-OS-sandbox pairing as baseline; the Dev Box is also listed as a pre-release device shipping later this year.

prediction_ref.short_label: Agent-harness vendors ship gVisor+OS-sandbox+VM containment specs by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Microsoft Scout sharpens the structural force the prediction rests on: an open agent harness adopted as the runtime and wrapped in a vendor's own enterprise controls rather than rebuilt. Scout, Microsoft's first always-on Autopilot personal agent embedded in Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint, is powered by OpenClaw, the open-source local-agent platform, and Microsoft layered governance on top: every Scout agent runs under a governed Entra identity with scoped credentials, audit trails, a continuous policy-conformance check, and Purview data-protection enforcement before data leaves, plus a Work IQ context layer. That is the same convergence logic the prediction names, where the hard differentiated work moves to the governance wrapper while the agent loop is a maintained open component. The gap to the prediction is dimensional: Scout's wrapper is identity, policy, and data-governance, not a published containment posture naming gVisor or an equivalent at the cloud tier and OS-native sandboxes at the laptop tier, and there is no standards-body agent-runtime-containment draft today, so this reinforces the open-core-plus-vendor-controls pattern without yet delivering the named per-OS-sandbox and per-product-VM containment specs.

prediction_ref.short_label: Anthropic files confidential S-1 with SEC by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today's IPO coverage reports the prediction's event has effectively happened well ahead of its Q2 2027 window: Anthropic confirmed last week that it has confidentially filed a draft S-1 with the SEC, after a May round valued it at $965 billion, up from $380 billion in February. A confidential draft S-1 is precisely the JOBS Act filing the prediction named as the trigger that begins the SEC comment process without public-float disclosure, and the move arrives inside roughly twelve months of the $965 billion Series H rather than next spring. The reporting also notes OpenAI is preparing its own confidential filing within weeks, situating Anthropic's filing inside the compute-thesis listing queue alongside SpaceX. The only thing short of full realization is procedural confirmation detail: the filing is confidential, so the public registration statement, the audited-financials cutoff, and the road-show timing the prediction's outer markers describe are not yet on the public record.

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The SpaceX IPO and the AI-lab listing queue keep the compute-disclosure question on the table the prediction expects the SEC to address. SpaceX fixed its IPO at $135 a share before its roadshow even begins, an unusual pre-commitment, selling about 555.5 million shares to raise roughly $75 billion at a valuation near $1.77 trillion, with pricing expected June 11; the print lands inside a crowded queue of compute-thesis listings, with Anthropic's confidential draft S-1 already filed and OpenAI reportedly preparing one. That concentration of compute-correlated issuance underwritten by the same syndicate banks is the disclosure-quality environment the prediction's concept release rides on. But today's news contains no SEC Division of Corporation Finance action: no concept release, no disclosure-granularity guidance on committed-compute-revenue versus cancellable-capacity-lease language, so the signal sits on the market-supply side rather than on the regulatory output the prediction is keyed to.
